Holes: ~33 Medi turns are '[speaking Arabic]'/'[speaking foreign language]' (05:28, 06:13-06:28, 26:46-30:50, 1:02:48-1:09:06) so several fixes there are inferred from Amal's recast only (rows 3,5,21,22,42,43,44 marked low/medium). 18:52-1:01:44 is mostly ASR Latin for both speakers (t- prefixes and 7/3 often dropped, e.g. hamasna 19:19, daya ti 46:42); I did not score those as errors. Pronunciation left out per S4: h for 7 in every 7ammas form (10:44, 12:39, 12:53, 13:22 - Amal recast each), ba7seb for ba3asseb 11:30, 'It's a three' 30:08, long-a in daaya2ni 44:52 and tetdaaya2i 51:16 (F2), shufeta 54:29, بندارة 08:32 (ASR of kundara), akhti 57:26 (ASR of ta5ti). Skipped: chat 21:17 't7ammastu hunaak' (he was reconnecting, no attempt); 1:08:21 he asked about singular after 30 and knew the rule; Medi corrected Amal at 49:59 (kaan drops b-). Chat 39:33 'e7na bnetwajja3 bsur3a' lacks the ma he said - her typo, not his error.

rows.amal_said: No، it's present، بس it's one، not group of things.
rows.why: For 'what excites you' (singular subject) he used the plural bey7ammsu; Amal: it's one, not a group, and typed bey7ammes.

rows.amal_said: Made. ... Past. He made me excited.

rows.amal_said: Mm. Get excited, not excite me or someone. ... It's the wrong verb. It's get excited, not excite.
rows.why: Command 'get excited' needs the get-form t7ammasi; he gave the make-form 7ammsi (excite someone). Amal: 'It's the wrong verb'.

rows.medi_said: Oh, you're right. Okay. Uh, tetamasi.
rows.why: He stacked a second t- (tet7ammasi) on the command; Amal: 'No T, just one T'.

rows.amal_said: This is why don't you get excited? Why aren't you excited now? ... we are using the adjective here because it's are.
rows.why: He negated the verb (ma bit7ammasi = why don't you get excited) where 'aren't you excited' is a state word, mish + participle; he then produced Lesh mish mithamsa.
shaare3 = street, she asked for 'road' and he switched to el-taree2; sheet: 'road / way / route | 6ariq | طريق' and 'street | Shaare3 | شارع'.
Transcript shows the make-form 7ammasna for 'we got excited'; Amal said Mm-hmm and her chat has t7ammasna, so the ASR may simply have dropped the t.

rows.english: I hurt someone / I get hurt

rows.medi_said: I, I can't use it 'cause I don't have the adjective.

ijr is feminine so the verb must be bt-; he had beywajje3, then wrongly changed the possessive (رجلك) before landing on رجله بتوجع.
'Sometimes I hurt you' needs the I-form bawajj3ek; he said the he-form beywajje3ek after ana. No spoken fix, her chat has bawajj3ek.
